DEPLOYMENT_CONTRACT_DRIFT.process_implication: Fixing QDRANT_URL alone would close this incident while leaving the process defect intact, so the next required variable will fail the same way. Wave 1 must make the deployment path enforce the contract, and Wave 6 must reproduce the environment from code rather than by hand.
DEPLOYMENT_CONTRACT_DRIFT.summary: The root cause is not simply a forgotten environment variable. The deployment contract exists but is not the deployment path actually used, while documentation and build evidence create the impression that the dependency is unnecessary.
DEPLOYMENT_CONTRACT_DRIFT.why_it_matters: Two independent failure modes compound here. First, the contract is not enforced on the path that ships, so a required dependency can be silently absent in production. Second, the documentation gap in .env.example plus the misleading 'self-contained' image label actively discourage a future operator from supplying the value. Anyone creating .env from the sample file and then running deploy.sh would also hit a contradiction, since deploy.sh requires a variable the sample omits.

W0.2_QDRANT_DEPLOYMENT.claim: Qdrant is required by the primary serving path, but the deployed Azure Container Apps revision does not provide QDRANT_URL, so configuration falls back to localhost:6333.
W0.2_QDRANT_DEPLOYMENT.code_predicted_behaviour: SUPERSEDED IN PART by a82f24b ('fix(agent): error path must not crash when the stack is down'), which hardens the failure path. It does NOT change the root cause: the new revision still carries the same 10 env vars and still has no QDRANT_URL, so retrieval remains unavailable. The earlier prediction was that agent.chat() catches the exception and returns HTTP 200 with status='error', has_evidence=False and plan={retrieve: False}. That predicted behaviour was NOT directly observed, because every retrieval endpoint requires auth and the probe was not bypassed.
W0.2_QDRANT_DEPLOYMENT.confidence_upgrade_condition: Authenticated Azure business-path probe once identity is available. That is the same capability Wave 1 unlocks, so it costs no separate work.
W0.2_QDRANT_DEPLOYMENT.contradicting_evidence: build-container.yml writes image evidence asserting mode = 'cloud-demo, self-contained (no Qdrant/Postgres/LLM gateway)'. That label is misleading: Dockerfile.api bundles only data/ and the demo user seeder. 'Self-contained' means no co-located service, not no network dependency. It creates a false belief that no Qdrant is needed, but it does not create a working non-RAG mode, so it does not overturn the verdict.
evidence: /ready constructs QdrantStore, whose __init__ runs a hard connectivity probe (get_collections) and raises ConnectionError when every candidate fails.
Note the asymmetry: QdrantStore.count() swallows exceptions and returns 0, so the failure comes from CONSTRUCTION, not from counting -- meaning any path that builds the store fails.
build_stack() is on the primary query/chat path: api.py calls it at lines 746/775/802/1519, and query() -> _query_impl() -> build_stack(). No branch bypasses it.
No non-RAG serving mode exists anywhere in the codebase.
scripts/deploy.sh declares QDRANT_URL in REQUIRED_VARS and FAILS if it is empty.
The compose deployment provides a Qdrant service explicitly (deploy/docker/compose.app.yml: depends_on qdrant, QDRANT_URL=http://qdrant:6333).
ACA revision ca-maia-api--0000006 carries 10 env vars and none is QDRANT_URL. Verified at runtime, not inferred from .env.example.
config.py:27 therefore resolves QDRANT_URL to the default http://localhost:6333, which does not exist in the container.
The app starts cleanly and /health returns 200: nothing touches Qdrant until a request needs the stack, so startup success carries no signal about retrieval.
W0.2_QDRANT_DEPLOYMENT.limitation: No authenticated Azure /chat request has yet directly observed the expected retrieval failure. The final link in the chain is inferred from code, not observed at runtime, which is why confidence is MEDIUM and not HIGH.
W0.2_QDRANT_DEPLOYMENT.revalidated_after_concurrent_change: A parallel process committed and deployed a82f24b while this investigation was running. The finding was re-checked on the live revision ca-maia-api--0000006 and is unchanged: 10 env vars, no QDRANT_URL, resolving to localhost:6333. Recorded here so the finding is not mistaken for an artifact of the older revision 0000005.
W0.2_QDRANT_DEPLOYMENT.root_cause: Manual ACA deployment bypassed the repository deployment contract and its REQUIRED_VARS validation. There is no ACA deployment automation anywhere in the repo; the only occurrence of 'containerapp' is a comment in build-container.yml. Every other deployment path (deploy.sh, docker compose) supplies Qdrant, so the cloud path is the sole exception.

W0.JWT_EPHEMERAL_SECRET.impact: Tokens and sessions are expected to become invalid after a process restart, because the runtime generates a new ephemeral signing key. With minReplicas=0 every scale-to-zero cycle is a restart. This claim is deliberately scoped to token/session invalidation on restart; it is NOT extended to a broader claim about every session mechanism, which the code has not been shown to support.
W0.JWT_EPHEMERAL_SECRET.observed: JWT_SECRET_KEY is absent on ACA revision ca-maia-api--0000006.
W0.JWT_EPHEMERAL_SECRET.root_cause_relation: Same deployment-control gap as QDRANT_URL: manual deployment bypasses required-configuration validation. deploy.sh lists JWT_SECRET_KEY in REQUIRED_VARS; the ACA revision does not set it.
W0.JWT_EPHEMERAL_SECRET.runtime_evidence: Startup log: 'RuntimeWarning: JWT_SECRET_KEY is not set -- using an ephemeral random key. All tokens/sessions will be invalidated on restart. Set JWT_SECRET_KEY in .env for production.' Observed in ACA console logs for revision ca-maia-api--0000006.
W0.JWT_EPHEMERAL_SECRET.why_not_now: Setting it by hand would add yet another manually-managed static secret, deepening exactly the problem Wave 1 exists to remove. Wave 1 must solve it properly through identity and a secrets architecture.
